items.title: 61539_Butter Jackson oral history interview
items.q: So I had talked to Clarence Paige, one of the saxophone players in Zach's band,

ctx.x: Yeah. So you got your 50 -- you got your $60 a week instead?

Yes, I did. So I said, gee whiz. Now he called me and said, "I want you -- Do you need any money?" And I said, well, "Sure." So I had talked to Clarence Paige, one of the saxophone players in Zach's band, and I'm young, I don't know, I'm dumb, I'm fresh from Springfield. I didn't know what to ask him for. So Clarence said, "Ask him for $100. He's got plenty of money." So I asked McKinney for $100. And do you know he sent me the $100.

So he sent me a train ticket and I got on the train -- I had never been on a train before because in Zach's band we traveled in automobiles and some of those cars if you would see them, you wouldn't believe. Those cars. I drove the baggage car, a little baggage car. It was a four cylinder Dodge. It couldn't go over 50 miles an hour and I drove it once all the way from [Camden], Ohio, to Philadelphia over the mountains.
